subject: Clarify: default retention for streaming fragments, prompts, and final outputs
messages:
From: Diane Schaefer <diane.schaefer@brightbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <sec@brightbank.com>
Date: 2025-10-05 09:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify retention for streaming sessions and prompt storage

Hi Marcus,

Quick question from our security team about how Redwood treats streaming interactions. We have two specific asks: 1) while a streaming response is being generated, are intermediate fragments (partial token buffers) ever persisted to disk or logs by default? 2) do the original user prompts (the raw user input) get stored by default along with final outputs?

We're evaluating default retention windows and need concrete examples to include in our Data Processing Assessment. Can you outline typical default behavior for hosted Redwood API (non-dedicated) and note any exceptions (debug logs, forced-profile traces, or legal hold scenarios)?

Thanks,
Diane
Diane Schaefer
Head of Platform Security, BrightBank

---
On Oct 5, 2025, at 10:04 AM, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Schaefer <diane.schaefer@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-05 10:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify retention for streaming sessions and prompt storage

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers first, then a short set of examples below. Attaching a small capture-flow JSON and our retention matrix for reference.

Short answers:
- Intermediate streaming fragments: ephemeral by default. The serving runtime keeps an in-memory buffer for partial tokens and a short-lived write-ahead buffer for crash safety, but we do not persist streaming fragments to customer-visible logs unless crash diagnostics are enabled for a specific session (opt-in or on-demand via support ticket).
- Raw user prompts: final request payloads (the user-provided prompt) are stored by default in the request store for hosted API customers and are retained under our default retention window. We treat prompts as request artifacts.
- Final outputs: model responses (finalized completions) are stored as output artifacts and follow the same default retention window as requests.

Default retention windows for hosted API (typical):
- Requests (prompts, metadata): 30 days
- Final outputs (generated completions, final transcripts): 30 days
- Streaming fragments and transient KV cache items: ephemeral (kept in memory; flushed on session end), not stored long-term by default

Exceptions / notes:
- Debug traces or explicit session traces: if a customer enables verbose tracing for troubleshooting, we may persist richer session artifacts for a limited time; this requires customer opt-in and is logged as a special retention flag.
- Legal hold / eDiscovery: if an enterprise contract includes a data-hold clause, retention windows can be extended and are managed through the legal/CS playbook.
- Dedicated/Private deployments: customers can configure retention windows at deployment time; on-prem installations are subject to the customer's storage config.

Examples:
1) Simple API call (non-streaming): user sends a prompt -> request and final output stored in default request/output stores; auto-pruned after 30 days.
2) Streaming chat: user receives tokens incrementally; intermediate fragments are in-memory until stream end. On normal completion, only the final assembled transcript is written to outputs (retained 30 days).
3) Crash scenario: short write-ahead buffer may be persisted for post-mortem; these crash artifacts are automatically purged within 7 days unless flagged for engineering investigation (requires customer consent).

I'll loop in Kimberly for legal wording and Rishi for any ML/trace exceptions we should call out. Happy to run a short example export for your team to review.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify retention for streaming sessions and prompt storage

Diane — adding a short formal summary you can drop into your assessment.

Formal summary (recommended language):
"By default, Redwood's hosted API retains request payloads (user prompts) and final model outputs for a 30-day window to support customer debugging and analytics. Transient artifacts generated during streaming (intermediate token fragments and in-memory KV caches) are not persisted to long-term storage and are considered ephemeral. Exception paths (verbose tracing, crash post-mortem buffers, or contractual legal-hold extensions) are documented and available on request; these require explicit opt-in, support coordination, or contractual terms. Evidence of deletion and retention actions can be supplied through Redwood support for compliance audits."

If you need this on company letterhead or with a signature block from Legal, we can route to Legal Ops.

— Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Compliance, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Marcus — this is perfect, thanks. Two quick follow-ups: 1) can you provide an example API call and the exact fields we should expect in an export for proof-of-deletion (we want to show auditors how to verify a purge), and 2) can you confirm the default 30-day window applies to embedded content (images or files attached to prompts) or are those treated differently?

If easier, a short export example and a statement that attachments follow output retention rules would be ideal.

Best,
Diane
